ca:["$","p",null,{"children":"The third method needs no classical reference. For each parity, take the values at noise factors 1, 1.5, and 2, divide out the learned readout damping (TREX), fit an exponential in the noise factor, and extrapolate to zero noise. Parities that change sign or are nearly zero get a straight-line fit. Subtracting the variance needs a reliable estimate of it, which is easy for raw and rescaled parities but not for the output of a nonlinear fit with clipping and fallbacks. PEA therefore uses the other standard way to remove the bias of a square.
